gap: No retrieval benchmark evaluates version selection over continuously amended legal text at clause granularity: no resource pairs time-stamped queries with ground-truth in-force versions of overlapping, near-duplicate amended clauses and measures retrieval of superseded or not-yet-in-force text. Legal-domain temporal work is either conceptual/prescriptive (explicitly without empirical comparison) or multiple-choice over normative-act relationships without source-text retrieval; temporal retrieval benchmarks with temporal-accuracy metrics exist only for ESG disclosures and financial filings; regulatory retrieval benchmarks have no target dates at all.

why_unaddressed: The temporal QA survey states legal QA datasets are static and do not address the temporal dynamics of legal knowledge; the legal-retrieval framework that formalizes the requirement ('diachronic blindness', 'bitemporal correctness') states explicitly that it reports no benchmarked empirical comparison and is formal and diagnostic; the legal benchmark that encodes temporal validity is a multiple-choice diagnostic that does not evaluate retrieval of source text; the point-in-time evaluation protocol with a temporal-leakage metric exists only for financial filings; and the regulatory retrieval benchmark has no target-date or version dimension.
research_question: On a corpus of continuously amended statutes/regulations with near-duplicate successive versions, does valid-time-aware (as-of) temporal re-ranking reduce retrieval of superseded or not-yet-in-force clauses, and improve answer accuracy, compared with semantic-only retrieval and with a recency-decay baseline?
potential_experiment: Construct a version-level benchmark from a jurisdiction with machine-readable amendment metadata (e.g., EU legislation under ELI, which encodes date of entry into force and date of applicability): retrieve clauses from a versioned corpus where successive versions are near-duplicates; annotate queries with a target date and the ground-truth in-force clause version, deliberately including target dates whose authoritative version is not the latest; evaluate semantic-only, recency-decay, hard as-of filtering, and valid-time gated re-ranking, reporting version-level temporal contamination alongside answer accuracy.
verification_required: Re-run literature searches (the paper budget for this session is exhausted) for any amended-statute retrieval benchmark, and confirm that passage/clause-level validity metadata (not only legislation-level dates) can be extracted for the chosen jurisdiction and corpus snapshot.
